title: kubeconfig: client-key-data holding an encoded PEM private key
summary: A synthetic kubeconfig whose users entry carries client-key-data as one long base64 line that decodes to a PEM private key block (synthetic non-key material).
rationale: The PEM frame is hidden inside an encoded value, so nothing in the visible text names a private key except the field name. The decoded block is the existing generic:private-key family (#54); encoded embedded material and decoded-source mapping are #94 and stay with the downstream owners.

expectation.rationale: Flag the client-key-data value (the whole encoded line). The client-go types say client-key-data contains PEM-encoded data from a client key file and mark it with datapolicy security-key. The expected span is on the encoded text as it appears; how a consumer decodes it and maps a decoded finding back is out of scope here. That the serialized text encoding is base64 is recorded as unresolved in the contract: the fixture is authored in that conventional form.

sources.supports: ClientKeyData contains PEM-encoded data from a client key file for TLS. Overrides ClientKey; ClientKeyData []byte with datapolicy security-key.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. Product masking envelopes, decoded-source mapping and action policy stay with the downstream repositories.
